The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

Herd immunity can be understood through the analogy of a computer network firewall. Just as a firewall protects a network from malicious viruses, herd immunity protects a community from infectious diseases. If a large enough portion of the population (computers) is vaccinated or immune (protected), the spread of the disease (virus) is significantly hindered. This creates a barrier that prevents the infection from reaching those who are not protected, much like how a secure network prevents an infected computer from spreading malware to other uninfected machines.
